concepts.title: Maps: Meaning, Types and Their Uses
concepts.definition: A map is a representation of the whole or part of the earth's surface drawn to scale on a plane, classified by scale into large scale cadastral and topographical maps and small scale wall and atlas maps, and by theme into physical and cultural maps serving planning, navigation and education.
concepts.key_idea: Maps carry a title, scale, direction, legend or key and conventional signs, so that any reader can decode the surface features accurately.

concepts.title: Globes, Aerial Photographs and Remote Sensing as Map Sources
concepts.definition: A globe is the truest representation of the earth without scale distortion, aerial photographs taken from aircraft and satellite images from remote sensing supply raw data from which maps are compiled, and modern GIS stores and analyses these map layers digitally.
concepts.key_idea: Photographs and satellite data reduce field work and update maps quickly, while GIS overlays thematic layers for spatial analysis.

concepts.title: Essential Elements and Conventions of Map Language
concepts.definition: Every map carries five essential elements of title, scale, direction shown by north line, legend or key of conventional signs, and date or source of data, and its language of symbols, colours and lines lets complex surface information be read quickly and uniformly.
concepts.key_idea: North is conventionally placed at the top and symbols are standardised so that any trained reader interprets the map identically.
